In Europe, the hotel brands most commonly considered for **branded residences** are **Marriott** brands such as **Ritz-Carlton**, **St. Regis**, **JW Marriott**, **W**, and **EDITION**; **Accor** brands such as **Raffles**, **Fairmont**, **Sofitel**, **SLS**, and **SO/**; and luxury operators like **Four Seasons**, **Mandarin Oriental**, **Kempinski**, **Six Senses**, and **Rosewood**.[3][4][10][12][15]

If you are looking at the **most frequently cited active brands in Europe**, the research points especially to **Marriott overall**, with **Radisson Blu** highlighted as the most active individual hotel brand in one Europe-focused market overview, and **YOO**, **Kempinski**, **JW Marriott**, **Six Senses**, and **Mandarin Oriental** also appearing among the leading European brands depending on how the market is measured.[1][2][3][9]

A practical way to think about the market is:

- **Luxury/ultra-luxury:** Four Seasons, Mandarin Oriental, Rosewood, Aman, Six Senses[12][15][19]
- **Major global hotel groups:** Marriott, Accor, Hilton, Hyatt, IHG[10][15]
- **Common branded-residence sub-brands in Europe:** Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, JW Marriott, W, EDITION, Raffles, Fairmont, Sofitel, Raffles, Kempinski, Radisson Blu[3][4][10][12][15]

Europe also has a notable share of **regional hospitality brands** used for residences, including **Falkensteiner**, **Martinhal**, **Club Med**, and **Lefay**.[4]
